title: AI-Powered Energy and Water Optimisation Platform for Water Infrastructure
summary: Gatisheel is an IoT-, SCADA- and AI-enabled platform for monitoring, automating and optimizing water infrastructure. It links water-flow and energy data to support efficient pumping, fault detection, remote operations and resource conservation.
search_text: Gatisheel is an IoT-, SCADA- and AI-enabled platform for monitoring, automating and optimizing water infrastructure. It links water-flow and energy data to support efficient pumping, fault detection, remote operations and resource conservation. Gatisheel is an IoT-, SCADA- and cloud-based platform for automating and remotely managing water infrastructure. It connects pumps, valves, flow meters, level and pressure sensors, energy meters, and existing PLC or automation systems to a centralized web and mobile platform. The system provides real-time monitoring, remote operation, automated scheduling and control, fault alerts, historical reporting and performance dashboards. Its control logic and predictive or AI-assisted analytics help operators identify abnormal conditions, inefficient operations and potential maintenance requirements. By correlating water flow with electricity consumption, the platform enables operators to monitor energy used per unit of water delivered or treated and identify opportunities to improve pumping efficiency. Role-based access supports the management of multiple assets and responsibilities. The platform is designed for retrofit and new installations across water-supply networks, pumping stations, water treatment plants, sewage treatment plants, irrigation systems, canal-control infrastructure and industrial water facilities. The submission identifies applications in pump-house automation, non-revenue-water analytics, lift-irrigation management, treatment-plant automation, canal-flow control and centralized multi-site operations. According to the provider, the technology has received technology approval from the Jal Shakti Vibhag, Himachal Pradesh. Supporting documentation was referenced but not supplied for verification. 1. Supports water conservation through real-time flow monitoring, automated control and detection of abnormal water use. 2. Improves energy efficiency by monitoring pump consumption and energy used per unit of water delivered or treated. 3. Enables remote supervision and control of geographically distributed infrastructure. 4. Reduces manual intervention, unnecessary site visits and avoidable equipment downtime. 5. Provides real-time alerts and historical performance data for operational planning and maintenance. 6. Supports centralized, scalable management of multiple water assets and locations. 7. May reduce indirect greenhouse-gas emissions through lower electricity consumption. 8. Improves operational visibility, accountability and service reliability. 1. Water supply and distribution systems 2. Water and sewage treatment plants 3. Pump houses and pumping stations 4. Irrigation and lift-irrigation systems 5. Canal gates and water-control infrastructure 6. Industrial water management 7. Municipal and urban water infrastructure 8. Smart cities and smart water networks 9. Large-scale agriculture and agri-enterprises 10. Multi-site utility operations Target users include government water and irrigation departments, public water authorities, urban local bodies, smart-city authorities, treatment-plant operators, industrial facilities, Water User Associations and utility-management companies. title: PathPal: Offline Edge-AI Assistive Mobility and Accessibility System
summary: PathPal is an offline, edge-AI assistive device that combines computer vision, OCR, currency recognition and multidirectional obstacle detection to provide real-time audio and haptic support for safer, more independent mobility and access to printed information.
search_text: PathPal is an offline, edge-AI assistive device that combines computer vision, OCR, currency recognition and multidirectional obstacle detection to provide real-time audio and haptic support for safer, more independent mobility and access to printed information. PathPal is an AI-powered assistive device developed by SmartEye3i Technologies Pvt. Ltd. to support the mobility, navigation and access to information of visually impaired users. It combines camera-based computer vision, offline edge-AI processing, optical character recognition, handwriting support, currency recognition and multidirectional ultrasonic obstacle sensing. The device detects hazards and other environmental information in real time and communicates results through multilingual audio feedback and differentiated vibration alerts. Its offline operation is intended to support use in crowded streets, markets and locations with limited internet connectivity. The technology integrates multiple assistive functions in a compact, rechargeable system rather than requiring separate single-purpose devices. According to the provider, PathPal has undergone more than 600 user interactions and field validations with visually impaired users, including pilots and paid pilots involving blind schools, NGOs and accessibility organizations. The provider also reports receiving an initial international order from Singapore and exporting PathPal to Geneva, Switzerland. The company reports securing INR 25 lakh in pre-seed funding from IHFC IIT Delhi and INR 16 lakh in grants and CSR support, as well as collaborations with Indian government stakeholders and T-Works. 1. Supports safer, more independent mobility for visually impaired users. 2. Provides access to printed and handwritten information through OCR and audio feedback. 3. Recognizes objects and currency. 4. Reduces reliance on caregivers for everyday navigation and information access. 5. Operates offline in low-connectivity environments. 6. Combines several assistive functions in one compact, rechargeable device. 7. Supports scalable deployment through institutions, government programmes, CSR initiatives and international partners. Blind schools and educational institutions; rehabilitation centres and healthcare settings; NGOs and disability-support organizations; government accessibility programmes; CSR deployments; public-space navigation; and international assistive-technology markets. Target beneficiaries include visually impaired individuals, blind students, elderly people with vision loss, rehabilitation beneficiaries, hospitals, government agencies and accessibility-focused institutions. The provider is seeking pilot projects, licensing arrangements, investment or financing, training or technical assistance, market-entry and local partnerships, and knowledge exchange. These partnerships are intended to support international expansion, strengthen edge-AI and sensor integration, and facilitate deployment in new markets.

title: Antiviral Pharmaceutical Composition Derived from Astraeus asiaticus Mushroom Extract
summary: An aqueous extract of the edible mushroom Astraeus asiaticus showed in-vitro activity against HSV-1, HSV-2, EV71 and Coxsackievirus A16, plus synergistic activity with acyclovir in tested HSV strains, including acyclovir-resistant HSV-2.
search_text: An aqueous extract of the edible mushroom Astraeus asiaticus showed in-vitro activity against HSV-1, HSV-2, EV71 and Coxsackievirus A16, plus synergistic activity with acyclovir in tested HSV strains, including acyclovir-resistant HSV-2. This technology concerns an antiviral pharmaceutical composition containing a polar or aqueous extract derived from Astraeus asiaticus, an edible mushroom found in Asia. In-vitro cell-based plaque reduction assays demonstrated antiviral activity against tested samples of Herpes Simplex Virus type 1 (HSV-1), Herpes Simplex Virus type 2 (HSV-2), Enterovirus 71 (EV71) and Coxsackievirus A16. The extract was evaluated at different stages of viral infection, including viral attachment, penetration and post-entry replication. Low cytotoxicity was observed in the tested Vero-cell model. Laboratory results also indicated synergistic antiviral activity when the extract was combined with acyclovir against tested HSV strains, including acyclovir-resistant HSV-2 samples. The technology is at an early development stage and has not undergone clinical testing or commercial deployment. Further work is required to standardize the extract, identify and characterize active compounds, confirm the mechanism of action, develop suitable formulations, and assess preclinical safety, efficacy, pharmacokinetics, dosage forms and manufacturing feasibility. The reported results are based solely on in-vitro laboratory studies and do not establish clinical safety or efficacy in humans. 1. Provides a natural-origin candidate for antiviral drug development. 2. Demonstrated in-vitro activity against HSV-1, HSV-2, EV71 and Coxsackievirus A16. 3. Demonstrated activity against both enveloped and non-enveloped viruses in laboratory studies. 4. Showed synergistic activity with acyclovir against tested HSV strains, including acyclovir-resistant HSV-2 samples. 5. Exhibited low cytotoxicity in the tested Vero-cell model. 6. Uses an aqueous extraction approach suitable for further process, formulation and preclinical development. 1. Antiviral pharmaceutical development 2. HSV-1 and HSV-2 research 3. Drug-resistant HSV research 4. Hand, foot and mouth disease drug research 5. Natural-product drug discovery 6. Antiviral combination-therapy research 7. Topical or oral formulation development Mahidol University is seeking pharmaceutical, biotechnology and research partners for joint research, pilot development, technology transfer, licensing, investment or financing, and knowledge exchange. Desired partner contributions include extract standardization; identification and characterization of active compounds; mechanism-of-action studies; formulation development; preclinical safety and efficacy studies; and GMP-compatible manufacturing-process development. Technology-transfer or licensing terms may be discussed according to the development plan, intended application, target territory and partner contribution. Any arrangement will be subject to institutional review, confirmation of territorial rights and a separate agreement.

title: Immunochromatographic Test Kit for Detecting Anti-Interferon-Gamma Antibodies
summary: A laboratory-developed immunochromatographic test strip detects anti-interferon-gamma antibodies in serum through visual test and control lines, providing a foundation for further clinical validation and in vitro diagnostic kit development.
search_text: A laboratory-developed immunochromatographic test strip detects anti-interferon-gamma antibodies in serum through visual test and control lines, providing a foundation for further clinical validation and in vitro diagnostic kit development. This laboratory-developed immunochromatographic test strip uses an antigen-based approach to detect anti-interferon-gamma antibodies in serum. Test and control lines provide a visual readout. The test-strip prototype was evaluated under laboratory conditions using positive and negative pooled serum samples. Separately, the underlying double-antigen sandwich ELISA method was evaluated using serum samples from 20 patients with adult-onset immunodeficiency and compared with indirect ELISA. These findings support further development, but large-scale clinical performance, regulatory authorization, and commercial deployment have not been established. The technology is intended for further development to support the assessment of patients with suspected anti-interferon-gamma-associated adult-onset immunodeficiency. It should not be presented as a standalone diagnostic test for immunodeficiency or as a measure of disease severity. Further clinical validation is required. 1. Provides a visually readable test-strip format for detecting anti-interferon-gamma antibodies in serum. 2. Has the potential to simplify testing and reduce dependence on specialized readers. 3. May support decentralized testing following clinical validation and applicable regulatory authorization. 4. Provides a foundation for further diagnostic-kit development, clinical evaluation, and manufacturing collaboration. 1. Anti-interferon-gamma antibody detection 2. Adult-onset immunodeficiency research 3. Clinical immunology and infectious-disease research 4. In vitro diagnostic-kit development 5. Potential decentralized testing following validation and regulatory authorization Joint research and technology transfer are sought. Potential partners include in vitro diagnostic manufacturers, biotechnology companies, clinical laboratories, hospital research teams, and research institutions with immunoassay and diagnostic-validation expertise. Collaboration may cover further clinical evaluation, diagnostic-kit development, and manufacturing. Any licensing or technology-transfer arrangement will be subject to confirmation of territorial rights and approval by the relevant rights holders.
